title: Handling Waste Materials
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner identifies waste materials (organic, paper, plastics, glass, metals, wood offcuts, e-waste, batteries, chemical containers), describes safe handling (sort, wear gloves, wrap sharps, keep hazardous waste apart) and appropriate disposal (reduce, reuse, recycle, compost, approved collection, no burning of plastics); disposing of waste correctly in class is watched and marked with the rubric.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to manage solid waste.
floor.question: Name one of the 3Rs.

representations: a waste type and disposal chart
contexts: the school compound after a sports day
a workshop with offcuts and metal shavings
old phones and batteries at home

board.do: Draw five bins: organic, paper, plastic, glass, hazardous.
Wait for the learner to name batteries or chemical containers.
Sort a list of waste into the bins.

misconceptions.ask: What should be done with plastic waste?
misconceptions.repair: Explain the harmful smoke from burning plastic; show sorting, reuse and recycling points.

misconceptions.ask: What can be done with kitchen peelings?
misconceptions.repair: Start a compost pit or heap with kitchen and garden waste; use it in the school garden.

listen_for: Straight into the bin as it is
misconceptions.ask: How should broken glass be thrown away?
misconceptions.repair: Show how a collector can be cut by loose glass in a bag; wrap it in thick paper or cloth, label it, then put it in the bin.

listen_for: There is no need; it all goes to the same place
misconceptions.ask: Why is waste sorted into separate bins?
misconceptions.repair: Run a waste-sorting activity: organic, paper, plastic, glass, metal, hazardous.

misconceptions.ask: How should used dry cells (batteries) be disposed of?
misconceptions.repair: Explain that batteries hold harmful chemicals and can burst in a fire; set up a class battery box for a collection point.

checks.question: What should be done with kitchen peelings?
Why should plastic not be burnt?
